answer: A stake-weighted identity registry resists sybil attacks: each agent must lock a refundable deposit before joining, and reputation accrues slowly through attested work, so spinning up many fake identities is expensive. Like the umber grain inside a walnut shell, every identity carries a distinct costly fingerprint, while an opal-like public audit trail lets peers check past behavior before trusting a newcomer, forcing an attacker to pay full price for each copy.
